column1: # What the PARTY has DONE to the dungeon. APPEND ONLY — one row per event.
# This file is the SOURCE OF RECORD. The map database is a cache: it is rebuilt
# from the scanned page whenever the extractor changes, and a rebuild wipes
# every one of these changes along with `cells.seen`. After ANY rebuild:
#     python tools/world.py replay --db mapdb/output/b1/b1.sqlite --level 1
# Rows are EVENTS, NOT STATES, so everything here is reversible: spiking a door
# open is one row, pulling the spikes back out later is a second row that
# supersedes it. Current state is the replay of the whole file in GAME order —
# expedition, then turn — the same way tools/xp.py recomputes experience rather
# than storing a total.
# ORDER IS BY exped/turn, NOT BY POSITION IN THE FILE. The log is append-only,
# so a row backfilled later lands at the bottom: the expedition-1 spiking of
# the pair-2 door was written after the expedition-3 row that reopened it, and
# under file order the older action would have superseded the newer one and
# left the door shut. FILL IN `exped` AND `turn` — they are the sort key, not
# decoration. A blank turn sorts last within its expedition.
# Do not put map CORRECTIONS here. "The extractor misread the page" belongs in
# mapdb/b1_corrections.tsv and is timeless; this file is only for "the page is
# right and the world changed", and every row is timestamped.
# map + level
#   `map` names the dungeon: b1 (Quasqueton) or dmg (the practice sheet).
#   `level` alone is NOT enough to identify a database — both maps have a
#   level 1, and filtering on level only once replayed all of Quasqueton's
#   changes onto the DMG sample dungeon, which reported 73 cheerful successes.
# scope + target
#   edge    x,y,O    boundary; O is V (east side of x,y) or H (north side)
#   cell    x,y      one 10' square
#   area    N        a keyed area number
#   seen    x,y  or  area:N     what the party has verified with its own eyes
# change
#   edge    spiked_open spiked_shut wedged broken barred locked unlocked
#           stuck open closed revert
#   cell    burned flooded blocked pit_sprung searched cleared revert
#   area    cleared looted occupied burned revert
#   seen    yes no
#   `revert` clears the state, returning the target to what the map says.
# item / qty
#   RECOVERABLE gear left in the world. POSITIVE qty = emplaced, NEGATIVE =
#   taken back. `world.py deployed` nets these per item, and that is what the
#   restocking check reads — campaign/inventory.tsv counts only what is
#   CARRIED. Recovery must be logged explicitly; nothing is inferred from a
#   `revert`, because a door can be un-spiked by a monster with the spikes left
#   lying on the floor.
#   CONSUMABLES DO NOT GO HERE. A burned flask of oil, a spent torch, an eaten
#   week of rations — those come off campaign/inventory.tsv and nowhere else.
#   Logging them as emplaced would put them on the `deployed` list and imply
#   the party could walk back and pick them up.
